correctness.rationale: Under 0<a,b<1, both substochastic killed matrices have determinant -b(1-a); their product is exactly lower triangular with repeated positive diagonal r and nonzero lower off-diagonal b(a+1-b). The nilpotent power proves exact even/odd survival. Every nonnegative product has spectral radius at least the square root of its determinant, and pi M 1 is bounded below by min(pi) times that spectral radius. For every nonalternating periodic schedule, cyclic rotation reveals a positive K_i squared factor, so Perron strict domination makes its escape exponent smaller. The lower triangular product has only one possible 1-to-0 crossing; all crossing locations have equal weight and the no-crossing mass is r^n. All boundary/normalization assumptions are explicit. CHECK.py performs 846 exact-rational finite consistency checks but the analytic argument establishes the infinite conclusions.

value.rationale: The positivity of the Markov off-diagonal transition weights gives a universal determinant-based optimal escape exponent, while the fair-product finite-horizon optimum fails under genuine Markov memory. The all-parameter asymptotic rescue, strict periodic equality characterization, sharp linear Jordan prefactor, and conditional uniform one-crossing time describe a natural survival/basin phenomenon with a coherent mathematical motivation. These are not table recomputation or a trivial rename of known fair-coin results.
